findings.title: Google Meet fallback throws when no destination calendar is configured
findings.body: When `destinationCalendar` is null or empty, destructuring leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` undefined, so accessing `.integration` throws before the booking can be created. This is the very case the fallback is meant to handle: a Google Meet location with no Google Calendar should switch to Cal Video rather than fail the booking.

findings.title: Co-host calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: The event is initialized with `destinationCalendar: null` when neither the event type nor organizer has a destination calendar. Optional-chaining this push then does nothing, even when `teamDestinationCalendars` contains calendars for collective co-hosts. Event creation consequently receives no co-host destinations, so those hosts do not get calendar entries.

findings.title: Only the first collective destination calendar is persisted for pending bookings
findings.body: This relation stores only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]`, so the other hosts' destinations exist only in the in-memory event. For bookings awaiting confirmation or payment, later confirmation flows rebuild the event from the booking's single destination-calendar relation and the organizer's calendar; they cannot recover the co-host destinations. Those hosts therefore never receive calendar entries for these bookings.

findings.title: Lark creates every host's event in the first destination calendar
findings.body: `EventManager` calls calendar creation once per destination using that destination's credential, but this method always selects `event.destinationCalendar[0]` and ignores the supplied credential ID. For a collective booking with multiple Lark credentials, later calls use the first host's calendar ID with another host's credentials, causing creation to fail or target the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Office 365 creates every host's event in the first destination calendar
findings.body: `EventManager` invokes creation separately for each destination credential, but this method always selects the first destination and does not use the credential ID to select the matching calendar. When collective hosts have different Office 365 credentials, later calls try to create an event in the first host's calendar using another host's credentials, so that host's event is not created.

findings.title: CalDAV silently skips host calendars other than the first destination
findings.body: Each destination is created with its own calendar credential, but this code filters that credential's calendars against only the first destination's external ID. For another host, that ID may not exist in its CalDAV account, leaving `responses` empty; the method still returns success, so the booking records a reference to an event that was never created.

findings.title: Google ignores configured destinations without a credential ID
findings.body: When a destination has an external ID but no `credentialId`, the event manager still supports it by selecting credentials by integration type. This lookup then finds no match and falls back to `primary`, so creation ignores the configured destination calendar and may write to the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Google update and delete cannot resolve a destination when the reference has no external ID
findings.body: When `externalCalendarId` is null or undefined, this lookup compares each real calendar ID to that same nullish value and finds nothing. Updates then send no calendar ID; deletes fall back to `primary` (the same faulty lookup appears at line 317), so an event in the configured destination can remain orphaned after cancellation. This affects callers or older references without an external calendar ID.

findings.title: Video booking references lose their credential ID
findings.body: This now sets `credentialId` to `undefined` for every non-calendar result, discarding the video result's credential ID. Cancellation code only deletes a video meeting when its booking reference has a credential ID, so meetings created through video integrations can remain active after their booking is canceled.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation still processes only the first calendar reference
findings.body: In the recurring-booking path, each future booking is reduced to its first calendar reference, and the code then uses the organizer's credentials rather than the credential for each reference. Collective bookings now have multiple references, including co-host calendars, so canceling all remaining instances can leave those calendar copies in place or attempt deletion through the wrong account.

findings.title: Organizations created without team billing no longer receive their slug
findings.body: This reverses the previous condition: when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false, the organization is now created without a `slug`; when it is true, the slug is assigned immediately as well as recorded as `requestedSlug`. In the non-billing configuration, organizations therefore lack the slug needed for their organization URL.
